area: Org following, server side: F1 (following lib + follow/unfollow, officer follower list, officer removal, the student's own followed-clubs list), F2 (follow fields and counts on /api/orgs, /api/orgs/[slug], /api/orgs/[slug]/profile, plus filter=following), F3 (invite-candidates opens on the club's followers), F4 (followed clubs in the feed lane, club names resolved with the service client)
alreadyDone: M1d is live (checked by read-only SQL, 2026-09-16). Latest migration is 20260916120000. org_followers has 7 rows, org_members 7, org_follow_firsts 7. There are 4 indexes, including org_followers_org_first_followed (org_id, first_followed_at DESC, id DESC) and org_followers_user_created (user_id, created_at DESC, id DESC). There is one policy, org_followers_select: user_id = auth.uid() OR org_member_role(...) IN (owner, admin). org_followers_source_check allows join, profile, discover and onboarding. Follower rows per org: SAE 1 (visible), the hidden test clubs 2/2/1/1. Posts with an org_id: 0.

Joining follows the club and leaving drops only the join-made follow, and both happen in database triggers (migration 20260916120000:802-843). join/route.ts, membership.ts (admitMember :248-315) and join-state.ts need no edit for following, and none is planned.

The profile route already has the hidden-club gate that half of C12 asks for: hidden and not a member returns 404, anonymous viewers included (src/app/api/orgs/[slug]/profile/route.ts:101-106). Its output is already written out field by field (:147-185).

Discover already uses the service client, leaves hidden clubs out and gives each row a join_state (src/app/api/orgs/route.ts:239-472). filter=mine is membership only and is read with the user client (:175-231).

invite-candidates exists. It is gated by requireInviteOfficer (owner/admin, hidden club returns 404, src/app/api/orgs/[slug]/invites/route.ts:195-240) and checks blocks both ways against the officer and the owner, failing closed (invite-candidates/route.ts:229-275). Nothing calls it yet: grep finds no client, and src/components/orgs/ does not exist.

criticResolutions: C1 (F4): the club-post limit groups posts with the new pure helper feedDiversityKey(post), which returns `org:<org_id>` or `user:<user_id>`. Nothing groups on the nullable org_id column alone. feed/route.ts:417 is replaced and a unit test covers it.

C2 (F4): both user-client org embeds are removed (feed/route.ts:221 and :254). Club names come from loadVisibleOrgCards with the service client and `hidden_at IS NULL`, joined in TypeScript. A hidden or unknown club gives org null, so the card shows the author. is_public stays in the output; hidden_at is never selected into the output or sent. orgs_select is not widened.

C3 (F1, F3): GET /followers and invite-candidates' followers mode both call loadHiddenUsers with the user client and drop those people with notIn in the query, before the limit. Both fail closed with 500 request_failed. hydrateUserCards is used only for identity fields, and a length mismatch returns 500 because it swallows errors. The invite sheet's existing block checks against the officer and the owner stay.

C4 (F1): DELETE /api/orgs/[slug]/followers/[userId] authorises owner/admin in TypeScript and deletes with the service client, per the migration's OFFICER REMOVAL contract (:195-223). No DELETE policy or grant is added. It refuses members with 409 member_follows. org_follow_firsts is kept, so removal works as a mute. A real ban (org_follow_blocks) is listed as an open question.

C5/C6 (F1, F3): the officer list and the invite sheet order by (first_followed_at DESC, id DESC), and the cursor carries both values. That matches the live index org_followers_org_first_followed. The student's own list orders by (created_at DESC, id DESC), matching org_followers_user_created. The cursor keeps the raw microsecond string, is quoted in the or() grammar, and is validated on decode.

C8 (F1, F2): org fields are named org_follow_state ("following"|"not_following"), org_follow_source and follows_since. The follower list keeps UserCard's person follow_state unchanged next to them. No route sends an org value under the name follow_state.

C9 (F1, server half): POST /follow on a hidden club returns 404 not_found to every non-member, platform admins included, and DELETE does the same unless the caller really was a follower. The client half (typing primaryOrgAction on JoinDisplayState, with a hidden row that shows no Follow button) belongs to F5a.

C10 (F4): followed club ids are an extra parameter to feedLaneOrFilter and postInFeedLane, not a FeedLane field, so trending/hashtags:92 and campus-request.test:197 compile unchanged. A viewer with no verified university gets a global lane, so following only changes their ranking. This is stated in the contract.

C11 (F2): list routes get counts from one `followers:org_followers(count)` embed on the existing service query. If the embed errors, the whole query errors and the route returns its existing 500 load_failed, never a quiet 0. Single-club routes use loadFollowerCount, a service head count that returns null on error.

C12 (F2): the hidden-club gate is already live at profile/route.ts:101-106 and stays first; the follower count is computed only after it. Signed-out viewers get a floored follower_count and viewer.org_follow_state null, which the client renders as Sign in to follow.

C13 (F1, F2): FOLLOWER_COUNT_FLOOR = 5 and publicFollowerCount() apply to every public count: discover and following rows, [slug], profile, and the follow/unfollow responses. Owner and admin of that club see the real number. The officer-only GET /followers and the removal route return the real count.

C15 (F1, F3): nothing an officer sees is sorted by created_at. Routes never write created_at or first_followed_at. POST and DELETE /follow share one rate-limit key, org-follow:<uid> (60 per 600s). org_follow_firsts is never deleted.

C17 (F1): the Terms check stays on POST /follow. Following discloses the student to the club's officers, and the join route has the same check. DELETE /follow and officer removal have no Terms check. The claims that following 'can never fail' or 'can't 403' must be dropped from F5a/F7 copy and specs, and F1's acceptance exercises 403 terms_required, 429 and 404.

C20 (F4): FOLLOWED_ORG_FILTER_CAP = 50, not 100, chosen against the combined URL budget (about 11.1 KB for authors, 1.9 KB for clubs, plus blocked/muted ids). The newest 50 follows are kept (ids arrive ordered by created_at desc), and truncation is logged with console.warn.

C24 (F1): the database CHECK already allows only join, profile, discover and onboarding. normalizeFollowSource accepts only profile, discover or onboarding from clients; anything else, 'join' included, becomes 'profile', so a client can never create a row the leave trigger would delete.

C25 (F1): GET /api/me/followed-orgs is rate limited (me-followed-orgs:<uid>, 60/60s) and paginated (limit up to 50, keyset cursor on created_at plus id). It always filters by user_id and drops hidden clubs.
C27 (F2): member_count becomes null on a failed read in discover (:426), [slug] GET (:292) and profile GET (:167), matching follower_count, instead of ?? 0. The page.tsx:127/:487 half belongs to F6.

C16 (server facts only): no route makes Join depend on following. Discover and following rows carry join_state and org_follow_state independently, and POST /join admits people who don't follow (the trigger adds the follow). filter=following includes member clubs and exposes `role` so the client can split 'followed, not joined'.
openQuestions: Officer removal of a follower is reversible in v1: the student can follow again, and their first-follow date survives. Recommended default: ship it as a mute. Do not build org_follow_blocks (the ban table sketched in the migration at :213-218) until Franky asks. The existing person block (public.blocks) covers harassment between two people.
Public follower-count floor. Recommended default: 5. Below 5, only the club's owner and admins see the number; everyone else sees nothing.

A student who joined before following has a follow with source 'join', which leaving deletes. Recommended default: POST /follow never upgrades an existing row's source. If the leave dialog offers 'Keep getting posts', the client calls POST /follow AFTER DELETE /join succeeds (a fresh profile row, same first-follow date).

Posts from a hidden club that still sit in the campus lane. Recommended default: show them as the author's post with org null (what non-members see today under RLS; 0 club posts exist), rather than dropping them the way the events route does.
hazards: F2, F3 and F4 import F1's following.ts. Run F1 first, or pin the exact signatures in the F1 contract before running the others in parallel.

org_followers_select also admits every follower row of clubs the viewer owns or admins. Any user-client read of the viewer's own follows without .eq("user_id", viewer) silently returns the club's followers too. loadViewerFollowedOrgIds must always add that filter, and /api/me/followed-orgs must too.

Cursor timestamps have microsecond precision. Passing them through JS Date (milliseconds) or leaving them unquoted in .or() breaks the keyset: tied rows are skipped or repeated, or the filter fails to parse. Keep the raw string PostgREST returned.
Never filter hidden-club posts with .notIn("org_id", ...). SQL `NULL NOT IN (...)` is not true, so that would remove every personal post, which is all 21 live posts.

filter=mine has three callers: campus-home.tsx:465 (chat rail), campus-home.tsx:6997 (post-as-club picker) and CampusMobile.tsx:1517 (phone chats). F2 must leave that branch byte-identical, and follower_count must never be added to it.
Discover and following rows will carry a floored follower_count. Spec §5.3 still says browse cards must not render it; that is F5b/F5c's job.
Nothing is protected by the 5 floor against someone who watches the count change. That is inherent to public counts. The floor only stops a count of 1 from naming the one member.
The owner/admin role list exists in two places: the RLS policy org_followers_select and FOLLOWER_LIST_ROLES. Adding 'mod' later means changing both together.

Owners and admins can still delete a member row directly through PostgREST (org_members_delete). That fires the leave trigger and drops the member's join follow with no rate limit. The migration header documents this at :336-351; do not describe the removal route as the only path.
The feed now returns 500 if the service read of club names fails. It only runs when the page contains club posts, and there are 0 today.
Members of a hidden test club lose the club name on its posts in the feed; the posts show as the author's. This is deliberate, and only test accounts are affected.

Other routes still embed orgs under the user client (search/route.ts:166 for events, users/[handle]/reposts/route.ts:99, me/calendar :80, me/upcoming-events :51). They show private clubs without a name; nothing leaks. They are outside this area; flag them for feature-sentinel.
channels/route.ts:29-36 still looks up the club with the user client, so SAE non-members get 404 (C18). This belongs to F6/B26, not to these batches.

0 club posts and 1 visible club exist live, so the F4 follow and name branches have never run on real data. Positive-path checks must run on a Supabase branch or local stack, or be done by Franky. Agents do not write follows or posts on prod.
tooManyRequests (rate-limit.ts:133) returns {ok:false, error} with no `code`. Clients must detect 429 by status.

invite-candidates in followers mode filters `source <> 'join'` in SQL. It relies on the leave trigger deleting join rows; if that trigger is ever dropped, ex-members with a stale join row would silently vanish from the invite sheet.
